anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves all three facts in the intended direction: Before treated `deliver-nits` as an unrecognized grant, ignored the 10/10 caps, and rendered final at 1111111 with N1/N2 left take-or-leave (so no wave, no N3, final rendered before any closure lines), whereas After honours the retained course, dispatches fresh implementers for N1 and N2 under one checkpointed wave, pushes to 2222222, lets the fresh re-review mint N3 and pull it into the next wave without a new pick, and renders final only at 3333333 after `N1/N2/N3: resolved` closure lines, exact-head CI success and a clean local-equals-remote check, with merge left as an unexecuted numeric row.
